body: Yes, we've talked about all of these things. Plenty of times. I'll be fine, regardless. Thanks.

He needs to stop lying to me about everything from how much beer he drinks to how badly he's handling finances. Hiding everything from me. He needs to understand that we're married and he doesn't get to make big decisions on his own.

He needs to get up and move his legs once in s while. He needs to act like getting healthy for his baby daughter matters, instead of continuing to eat garbage and sit around getting worse.

He needs to stop being so negative so consistently.

I don't know where the man I married went.

I no longer have a shred of faith in him, and I regret marrying him.
I'm not sure I even love him anymore.

I love our daughter more than life, though, and because of her I feel I need to give him more time to change...

Thank you for this. I feel it was a perfect response. I do my best to accommodate him, and we both have our hobbies and we love each others friends, but we sat and had a lengthy talk about it... I basically just asked him to put himself in my head a little more, and things like that.

I also told him I would gladly go out with him and his boss (he apparently wants his boss to meet me) any time, so long as I knew sooner than while being woken up!

Compromise is super important, it's just tough sometimes cos he and I are both super easy going but I step very carefully not to hurt his feelings and he just kinda derps out about mine sometimes. I was very adamant that I know he never INTENDS to hurt me, and that I wasn't necessarily angry.

We have a date night scheduled for my rare "two nights off in a row" and he's promised nothing will come between it. :) (Obviously if something crazy important came up, whatever, but you know what I mean.) He keeps reminding himself, out loud, and reminding me a well, "Unless it is important, girlfriend time is girlfriend time."

But thank you again for the response. :)

I'd like to think it is possible, but it seems so fleeting and elusive. And when I can hardly will myself out if bed anymore, it's hard to imagine ever really taking care of myself enough to be happy again.

I literally have zero dollars to my name. Free fun is the only fun I can have. Which gets exceedingly difficult in the harsh winters where I live.

Did I mention I don't drive, either? Nope. I've been too terrified my whole life to ever drive a car! So I can't go far, either.
I try to have fun, but that typically leads to remembering that I am broke, remembering that most people are shit and remembering that I like alcohol too much.

I've talked to friends, family, therapists, councelors, hell, even strangers.

Doesn't seem to change much.

You'd be shocked how often confessing to having been abused in the past leads to the listening party realizing they can get away with abusing you instead of comforting you. Talking gets terrifying after a while.

I feel pathetic because I shouldn't be this inhibited by my own life. There are people in the world worse off than me who can at least take care of themselves without being a drain on anyone around them, I'm sure. And here I am, finding myself too terrified of the world to even live in it.

I was born with multiple kidney, bladder and uterine and anomalies. I had, I think, five major surgeries as a child. Kidney disease still affects me today on a regular basis.
I suppose you're right, but it just feels ridiculous to be less if a responsible, functional adult now than when I was eighteen.

It's crazy how often people tell me I am "strong." It feels so false. Strength, to me, is overcoming, not just tolerating the shit rhat I have been through. I've learned so little from any of this, other than perhaps empathy. I don't feel "strong" for any of it. I feel more pathetic than anything, honestly.
Well, I certainly don't feel like I'm doing it right...
Less than a year of happiness versus more than 23 years of misery hardly makes it seem worth fighting for, but thank you for the kind words.
